structure.note: Counted from the capture. Properties of the protocol exchange, not of the machine that ran it.

congestion.assumed_initcwnd_note: 10 segments x 1460-byte MSS (RFC 6928 default). Tunable per route; stated so a reader on a different setting can re-judge.

round_trips.note: Counted from observed direction changes in payload-bearing packets, not from a protocol model. A retry or a congestion stall therefore appears as a real extra trip.

rtt.observed_at: server (capture shares the server network namespace)
rtt.note: Interval between the SYN arriving and the SYN/ACK leaving, as seen at the server. This is a full round trip only when latency is symmetric: a delay injected on the client's egress happens before the SYN arrives and is invisible from this end.

timing.note: NOT a published figure. This ran on whatever machine took the capture -- a developer laptop or a shared CI runner -- which is not publication-grade. Only the structural fields are portable.

environment.path_note: TCP passthrough proxy in the path: haproxy:3.0-alpine

sockets.sample_interval_note: Sampled every ~200 ms for the duration of the capture.
sockets.method_note: Read from /proc/net/sockstat and ss while the run was in progress. Connections reach SYN_RECV by handshaking normally -- no synthetic half-open connections are manufactured, so these are the depths a server actually sees under load.
sockets.bytes_per_established_reason: No idle baseline was observed, or fewer than 5 loaded samples. Refused rather than published from a thin sample.
sockets.bytes_per_half_open_reason: Only 0 sample(s) caught a connection in SYN_RECV -- too few to divide memory by. Connections here reach that state by handshaking normally rather than being held half-open synthetically, so the state is genuinely brief. Deliberately manufacturing half-open connections would mean building a SYN flood tool, which is out of scope.
